subtopics.title: Summit Outcomes
subtopics.summary: The 16th India-Japan Annual Summit was held in New Delhi during the first official India visit of Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, from July 1 to 3, 2026. The summit produced outcomes in defence, economic security, energy, artificial intelligence, trade and disaster risk reduction. Some outcomes launch new programmes, while others are agreements to convene further meetings or to review existing arrangements.
facts: 16th India-Japan Annual Summit held in New Delhi; Japan PM Sanae Takaichi's first official India visit, July 1-3, 2026
Defence: agreement in principle on remaining technical aspects of UNICORN (Unified Complex Radio Antenna), the first Defence Co-Development Programme between the two countries
4th India-Japan 2+2 Ministerial Meeting to be convened later in 2026
Joint Declaration on Economic Security Cooperation adopted
Priority areas: semiconductors, critical minerals, ICT, pharmaceuticals, clean energy technologies
Cooperative Biogas for Growth Initiative launched; Japan supports India's objective of 1,000 Biogas and Organic Fertiliser Plants
AI Strategic Dialogue launched; Joint Statement on Artificial Intelligence Cooperation adopted
Trade: accelerate review of CEPA; work towards a target of ¥10 Trillion in Japanese investment in India
Memorandum of Cooperation signed supporting a USD 10 Billion investment package
Japan supports India hosting the 4th UN World Conference on Disaster Risk Reduction in 2030; carries forward the Sendai Framework 2015-2030

subtopics.title: India-Japan Partnership Beyond the Summit
subtopics.summary: Japan's support for Subhas Chandra Bose's Azad Hind Fauj, formed to fight colonial rule, is a historical link in the relationship. Japan is India's largest official development assistance donor and its fifth largest investor. The partnership also covers joint military exercises, a lunar space mission and several global initiatives.
facts: Subhas Chandra Bose established Azad Hind Fauj (Indian National Army) with Japanese support to fight colonial rule
Bilateral trade in 2025-26: $27.48 billion
Japan is the 5th largest investor in India (FDI)
Japan is India's largest Official Development Assistance donor since 1958
Joint exercises: Malabar (naval, with US and Australia), Milan (multilateral naval), JIMEX (navy), Dharma Guardian (army), SHINYUU Maitri (air force)
Space: Lunar Polar Exploration Mission (LUPEX), also called Chandrayaan-5
Global programmes: International Solar Alliance; Coalition for Disaster Resilient Infrastructure; LeadIT; India-Japan-Australia Supply Chain Resilience Initiative
Frameworks listed under Skill-Up: Indo-Pacific Oceans Initiative, SAGAR, MAHASAGAR, QUAD, ASEAN, BIMSTEC, UNCLOS, G4 for UNSC Reform

subtopics.title: Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail Corridor
subtopics.summary: The Mumbai-Ahmedabad High-Speed Rail is a flagship India-Japan project that uses Shinkansen technology and forms part of India's National Rail Plan 2030. The corridor runs from Mumbai in Maharashtra to Ahmedabad in Gujarat and also passes through Dadra and Nagar Haveli. Japan finances most of the cost through a JICA loan and will supply Shinkansen train sets for the line.
facts: Route: Mumbai (Maharashtra) to Ahmedabad (Gujarat); length 508.17 km
Length split: 348 km in Gujarat, 156 km in Maharashtra, 4 km in Dadra & Nagar Haveli
Stations: 8 in Gujarat and 4 in Maharashtra
Technology: Shinkansen; part of India's National Rail Plan 2030
Japan will provide India with 3 Shinkansen train sets, including the E10 and E3 series
India to become the 1st country outside Japan to adopt the E10 Shinkansen high-speed train, designed by JR East (Japan)
Funding: over 80% financed by Japan (JICA loan) at 0.1% interest, repayable in 50 years
Implemented by National High-Speed Rail Corporation Limited
Deadlines: Surat-Bilimora stretch by 2026; full corridor by 2028

subtopics.title: Green Hydrogen and the National Green Hydrogen Mission
subtopics.summary: Hydrogen is the most common element in nature but exists only in combination with other elements, so it must be extracted from compounds such as water. Green hydrogen is made by splitting water through electrolysis using an electrolyser powered by renewable energy, and the booklet says it is not commercially viable at present. The National Green Hydrogen Mission, with the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy as nodal ministry, aims to decarbonise sectors and build domestic manufacturing.
facts: Hydrogen is the most common element in nature but exists only in combination with other elements
Hydrogen has to be extracted from naturally occurring compounds such as water
Green hydrogen: water is split by electrolysis using an electrolyser powered by renewable energy
Green hydrogen is not commercially viable at present
Nodal ministry: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Objectives: decarbonise energy, industrial and mobility sectors; develop indigenous manufacturing; create export opportunities for green hydrogen and its derivatives
SIGHT: Strategic Interventions for Green Hydrogen Transition Programme
SHIP: Strategic Hydrogen Innovation Partnership (PPP for R&D)
Expected by 2030: Rs 1 lakh crore in fossil fuel import savings

quizzes.passage:
The relationship between India and Japan reaches back to the struggle against colonial rule. During that period, a leader of the freedom movement received Japanese backing for an army he set up to fight colonial rule, and this episode remains part of the historical link between the two countries. The 16th annual summit, held in New Delhi, is the latest meeting in a long series of engagements between the two governments, and both countries have built ties across several sectors since then.

Today the partnership spans investment, development and defence. Japan is a significant investor in India and has long supported its development through official assistance, a form of support that has been a long-standing feature of the relationship. The navies, armies and air forces of the two countries all take part in joint exercises. Cooperation has also reached space, where the two countries are working together on a lunar polar mission.

Beyond the bilateral framework, India and Japan coordinate on several global programmes, including efforts linked to solar energy and to infrastructure that can withstand disasters. They also back a trilateral initiative that strengthens supply chains with a third partner. Their engagement also sits within a wider set of maritime and regional frameworks. The partnership is also reflected in the outcomes of the summit itself.

options: A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A

quizzes.passage:
Hydrogen exists only in combination with other elements, so it has to be extracted from naturally occurring compounds before it can be used. Its colour labels, such as grey, blue and green, are linked to how it is produced. Green hydrogen is the category made by a process that uses electricity to split hydrogen from a compound, with the electricity supplied by a particular type of source.

India has built a national mission around green hydrogen. The mission aims to bring change to several sectors, including energy, industry and mobility, and it also seeks to develop manufacturing capacity within the country. Its goals include opportunities for selling the fuel and its derivatives abroad. The mission has components that support a transition programme and a partnership between government and private players for innovation. Its expected results include a reduction in fossil fuel imports, which is measured in money terms.

Taken together, these elements show that the mission covers production, domestic manufacturing and trade rather than a single activity. Its scope therefore reaches from the process used to make the fuel to the markets in which it could be sold. This wide scope means the mission is not limited to a single step in the supply chain.

questions.q: Which statement about the commercial status of green hydrogen is correct?
options: It is fully commercially viable across India
It is not commercially viable at present
It is viable only for export
It is viable only in rural areas

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
